mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly drop in the unemployment rate below 8.0% in three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, prompting expectations of higher growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in such periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the unemployment rate does not fall below 8.0% as predicted.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) over the same month indicates robust demand growth, which compresses discount rates and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: both GDPC1 and HOUST increase in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns do not rise significantly when both proxies increase concurrently (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below 90.0 during a late-cycle expansion regime signals supply contraction, fostering higher inflation expectations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 90.0 during a late-cycle expansion regime
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in such periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) despite the INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) and GDP (GDPC1) over the same month creates conflicting signals: higher rates reduce discount rates on equities while stronger demand may boost valuations, but the net effect typically produces negative S&P 500 forward returns within 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: both FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 increase in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns do not decline significantly when both proxies rise concurrently (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in the unemployment rate above 9.5% in three consecutive months signals labor market weakness, dampening growth expectations and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not turn negative when UNRATE exceeds 9.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates robust economic growth, which lowers discount rates and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in periods of sustained GDP growth are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) and unemployment (UNRATE) over the same month creates conflicting signals: higher rates reduce discount rates on equities while weaker labor markets may lower growth expectations, typically resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE increase in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns do not turn negative when both proxies rise concurrently (t-test p > 0.05).
